userStories.title: Enforce self-contained writing standard across all documents
userStories.description: As a developer, I need every document to be fully understandable by someone with zero prior context — no implicit knowledge, no 'as discussed', no abbreviations without expansion — so that any person or AI reading a single document can understand it completely without needing to read the conversation or session that produced it.
acceptanceCriteria: Create docs/WRITING-STANDARD.md that defines the self-contained writing rules: (1) Every document must open with a 'Background' section that explains the full situation from scratch — what project this is, what problem exists, why this document was created (2) Never use phrases that assume prior context: 'as mentioned', 'as discussed', 'the above issue', 'this problem', 'we decided' without restating what was mentioned/discussed/decided (3) Every acronym and abbreviation must be expanded on first use, even project-internal ones (4) Every reference to another document must include both the relative path AND a one-sentence summary of what that document says — never just a bare link (5) Every technical term specific to this project must be defined inline or linked to a glossary entry (6) When describing a decision, always restate the full problem context, not just the solution

Update ALL templates to include a 'Glossary References' field at the bottom listing any project-specific terms used, with definitions or links to docs/GLOSSARY.md

Create scripts/check-writing.sh that scans documents for: (1) banned phrases ('as mentioned', 'as discussed', 'see above', 'the issue', 'we agreed' without full restatement) (2) bare links without summary descriptions (3) undefined acronyms (acronym detected but no expansion within the same document) (4) missing Background section (5) documents under a minimum content threshold (too short to be self-contained) — outputs a quality report with line numbers and suggestions

userStories.title: Create role profiles for solo full-stack developer

acceptanceCriteria: Create roles/ directory with INDEX.md

Create roles/product.md — Product Owner perspective: user value, priority, market fit, feature scope, success metrics. Checklist: Does this solve a real user problem? Is the scope minimal viable? How do we measure success?

Create roles/architect.md — Architect perspective: system design, tech stack choices, scalability, maintainability, 200-line convention compliance. Checklist: Does this fit the existing architecture? Will this scale? Are dependencies justified?

Create roles/backend.md — Backend Developer perspective: API design, database schema, business logic correctness, error handling, performance. Checklist: Is the API consistent? Is the data model normalized? Are edge cases handled?

Create roles/frontend.md — Frontend Developer perspective: UI/UX, component design, accessibility, responsive design, state management. Checklist: Is this intuitive? Does it work on mobile? Is state managed simply?

Create roles/data.md — Data Engineer / AI Scientist perspective: data pipelines, data quality, ML model design, training data, analytics. Checklist: Is the data pipeline idempotent? Is the model evaluation rigorous? Is data privacy respected?

Create roles/devops.md — DevOps perspective: CI/CD, deployment, infrastructure, monitoring, logging, disaster recovery. Checklist: Can this be rolled back? Is there monitoring? Are secrets managed properly?

Create roles/security.md — Security perspective: authentication, authorization, input validation, dependency vulnerabilities, compliance. Checklist: Is input sanitized? Are permissions least-privilege? Are dependencies audited?

Each role file follows a consistent structure: [Role Name] [Perspective — what this role cares about] [When to Activate — task types that trigger this role] [Review Checklist — questions to answer before approving work] [Red Flags — patterns that should raise concern from this role's viewpoint]
